newsitem.title: CANADA: One Seaway lane stays open after ship runs aground.
newsitem.headline: One Seaway lane stays open after ship runs aground.

text.p: One of the St. Lawrence Seaway's two lanes remained open to vessel traffic on Thursday after the Canadian Mariner ran aground Wednesday, a Seaway spokeswoman said.
"The Seaway's not blocked, traffic's going through one lane rather than two," St. Lawrence Seaway Authority spokeswoman Sylvie Moncion said in French.

No one was injured when the Canadian Mariner ran aground at Alex Bay near Brockville, Ontario, at 1030 EDT Wednesday. Barges unloaded part of its 25,060 wheat cargo Thursday to allow the ship to float up from the river bottom, she added.
"I heard it was an engine problem but I've been unable to confirm that," Moncion said.
The ship is owned by Upper Lakes Shipping of Toronto and was contracted by Seaway Bulk Carriers of Winnipeg, she said.
"The ship is insured. I don't know the extent of the damage," Seaway Bulk Carriers traffic manager Brian McAdam said.
The vessel was to transfer its cargo to an ocean vessel in Quebec City, Canadian Wheat Board spokesman Jim Pietryk said.
"We moved some barges to unload some wheat and that grain will move to Prescott (Ontario)," Pietryk said.
The Canadian Mariner may reload the transferred wheat in Prescott and proceed to Quebec City, he said.
"It may delay the shipment, depending on how long it takes," Pietryk said.
The ocean vessel's destination was not disclosed.
